newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse says starts workforce review.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse says starts workforce review.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp has begun a review that may result in workforce reductions at its corporate headquarters in downtown Pittsburgh and its Energy Systems headquarters in nearby Monroeville, Pa., company spokesman Kevin Ramundo said on Wednesday.

The positions under review are "related to support activities and general administrative activities" in departments including legal, communications, strategic planning and environmental affairs, Ramundo said.
He said the review was related to Westinghouse's sale of its defense electronics and office furniture units within the past year.
In addition to the corporate and energy unit headquarters, a power generation facility in Orlando, Florida, is under review. Employees received notice of the review this week, Ramundo said.

"The industry and technology group is a smaller and much more focused group than it was a year ago," he said. "We have a resulting opportunity to take a look at how we provide support services, and perhaps do it more cost efficiently."
Any jobs that are eliminated will be phased out by the end of the year. The review covers all 500 workers at corporate headquarters and about 500 workers at Energy Systems headquarters.

Ramundo said the review does not affect Westinghouse's plan to separate its industrial and broadcast businesses. The company, which acquired CBS Inc last November, is expected to announce its separation strategy in the fourth quarter.
Ramundo said there is no target number of jobs to be eliminated. Westinghouse has reduced its workforce by about 24,600 employees since 1993.
